plan.notes: Source: the official Brooklyn College four-year degree map for Computer Science, B.S., Bulletin Year 2018-2019, published by the Center for Academic Advisement and Student Success: http://www.brooklyn.cuny.edu/web/about/offices/caass/degree-maps/DM-computer-science-bs-2018.php. Course codes, titles, credits, and semester placement transcribed 2026-09-30 from that official map; course titles cross-checked against the official CIS department resources page (https://www.brooklyn.edu/cis/undergraduate-computer-science/) and the official Brooklyn College course inventory (websql.brooklyn.cuny.edu). True credential verified as Computer Science, B.S. (NYSED code 01991) on the current official program page https://www.brooklyn.edu/academics/programs/computer-science-bs/ (curriculum reflects the 2026-27 academic year); the major course set required by the current 2026-27 bulletin (CISC 1115/1170, 2210, 3115, 3130, 3140, 3320, 3305 or 3310, 3142, 3220 or 3230, 4900 or 5001, 2820W or PHIL 3318W, three additional 3000-4899 CISC courses, MATH 1201/1206 and 2501 or 3501) matches the courses sequenced in this map. Caveats: (1) The 2018-2019 degree map is the latest official term-by-term 120-credit sequence Brooklyn College has published for this program; no official 2026-27 four-year degree map was found, so catalog_year reflects the source document's bulletin year, not 2026-2027. (2) CISC 3305 (Computer Organization) is inactive and no longer offered per the CIS department course listing; current students take CISC 3310 (Principles of Computer Architecture) for the organization/architecture slot. (3) The official map lists the CISC 3305/3310 slot at 3 credits; confirm the current credit value with an advisor. (4) Per the official map's degree details: 42 Pathways credits + 56 major credits + 22 general-elective credits = 120 total. MATH 1011 is categorized as Pathways Required Core in the map (and so counts as 'general' here) even though calculus feeds the major. (5) B.S. degree requirement carried on the map: candidates must complete at least 60 credits in science and mathematics, including at least 24 advanced credits (courses numbered 2000 and above) in Computer and Information Science completed at Brooklyn College with a grade of C or higher in each course. (6) MATH 1011 placement note from the official map: depending on math placement, some students may be required to take MATH 1021 and MATH 1026 in a two-term sequence in lieu of MATH 1011; see an advisor to confirm placement.
